episodes.173957: A compact but strong upper level low pressure system dropped southeast across New Mexico on the 27th. Cold temperatures aloft and abundant low level moisture were able to create a modestly unstable environment within an atmosphere of strong wind shear. The combination of these features created strong thunderstorms on the afternoon and evening of the 27th. One of these storms produced ping ping ball size hail as it moved over Cee Vee (Cottle County). Lingering moderate rain showers early in the morning of the 28th generated a brief period of severe wind gusts near Brownfield (Terry County). A Texas Texas University West Texas mesonet site near Brownfield measured severe wind gusts from 0603 CST through 0607 CST with a peak gust of 65 mph.
episodes.174643: A meandering frontal zone was across North Central Florida as surface high pressure wedged an axis southward across GA. The onshore gradient between these two features produced gusty winds and enhanced low level isentropic lift near the meandering front which produced periods of heavy rainfall across portions of the coast and NE FL.
episodes.174781: The wet trend continued by the end of the month as another TUTT approaches the area. At first, this mid to upper level feature combined with moisture being pulling from the deep tropics into the region. Later in the period, a tropical wave was added to the mixture, further increasing moisture content and instability. A Flash Flood Watch was issued due to the excessive rainfall expected.
episodes.176557: A stationary front produced heavy showers for the territory that produced flash flooding across Tutuila on the 26th and 27th of October.

Emergency managers reported flooding along Baldorioty Avenue in Ponce. Four people were trapped in their cars, but all of them were rescued.

Emergency managers reported flooding along road PR-3 in Guayama.
Emergency managers reported a mudslides affecting road PR-3 in direction to Maunabo near a business called La Roca. A significant hole was created by the mudslide in this road.
Emergency managers reported that Rio Inabon was out of its banks near Mercedita Airport. Road PR-1 was closed due to flooding.
Emergency managers reported that a house was flooded near Road PR-13 in Rio Grande.
A report received by the 911 call center indicated that a residence was being affected by flood waters near Laura Navarro School, before a restaurant called Casaju. No one was trapped in the house.
A report from social media showed flash flooding occurring at road PR-184, km 5.0 in Barrio Jagual, Patillas. Several cars were trapped in the waters.
A bridge was washed away by a water surge in Patillas, road PR-7759 in Sector Los Barros.

Emergency managers reported people trapped in two cars when they tried to cross a flooded area. The flooding was caused by Rio Blanco being out of its banks, at Road PR-31, in the exit toward Highway PR-52.
A mesonet station measured 3.71 inches of rainfall in 2 hours.
Local broadcast media relayed a photograph of hail up to ping pong ball size.
